newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan wholesale pork prices plunge on export ban.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan wholesale pork prices plunge on export ban.

text.p: Taiwan's wholesale pork prices plummeted by as much as 61 percent on Thursday after the government announced an outbreak of hog foot-and-mouth disease and temporarily banned all pork exports.
Traders in Taiwan's main wholesale market in the capital Taipei said prices fell most dramatically in southern Taiwan, the island's primary hog growing area.

The average wholesale price for a kilogram of fresh pork in Kaohsiung was quoted at T$18 (65.4 U.S. cents) at the close of trading, down 61 percent from T$46 (US$1.67) before the news was announced, traders said.
The impact was somewhat less dramatic in Taipei, where one kg of wholesale fresh pork was selling for T$30 (US$1.09) at the close of trading, down 36 percent from T$47 (US$1.71).

The cabinet-level Council of Agriculture announced on Thursday that it was banning all exports of fresh and frozen pork temporarily due to an outbreak of the deadly contagious foot-and-mouth disease among pigs in nine counties.
Taiwan's consumer watchdog group, saying the outbreak would hit pork sales and prices, urged consumers to avoid buying pork products that had not been certified as safe by the government.

Grain importers said the crisis likely would trigger major reductions in Taiwan's feed corn imports, with most estimating the downturn at 1.2 million tonnes or 19 percent of the island's annual imports of 6.5 million tonnes.
Taiwan has been importing almost all of its corn from the United States, although recent high U.S. prices have prompted some importers to look to alterative sources in South America.

Japan, which is Taiwan's largest pork export market, has strict rules against importation of pork from regions known to be affected by the disease and was expected to impose its own ban on shipments from Taiwan, experts said.

Japan has been importing 16,000 tonnes of Taiwan pork a month despite imposition of an "emergency" import tariff to limit imports and protect local breeders. Taiwan's pork exports to Japan comprise about 69 percent its total pork exports.
South Korea also is a major importer of Taiwan pork.

The Taiwan council estimated that Taiwan breeds 14 million hogs per year. According to a 1994 survey, the industry was worth T$89 billion (US$3.24 billion), or about 20 percent of Taiwan's farm market and 60 percent of the livestock sector.
Taiwan's pork industry employs 700,000 people, including 100,000 pig farmers, the council said.
